# Individual life underwriting manual (starter edition)

This is the whole of the written practice. Rate every application from it. Where it says *refer to underwriting judgement*, the manual has nothing more to give you.

## 1. Decision vocabulary

Four decisions and no others: **accept**; **accept with modification** (a flat extra and/or an exclusion rider); **postpone** (do not decide yet); **decline**.

## 2. Rating classes and the debit bands

Add the debits from sections 3-14 and read the class off the total: 0-49 Standard | 50-99 Table 2 | 100-149 Table 4 | 150-199 Table 6 | 200-249 Table 8 | 250+ Decline.

A decline band in any single table declines the file whatever the total comes to. Three preferred classes sit above Standard. Each needs **zero debits** and, in addition:

- **Standard Plus**: BMI 27.9 or under; BP 138/88 or under and untreated; TC 240 or under with ratio 5.0 or under; A1c 6.4 or under with no diabetes diagnosis; tobacco never or quit over 5 yr; 0 moving violations and no DUI in 5 yr; occupation class A or B; no hazardous avocation; at most 1 family-history event; no sleep apnea, no alcohol history, normal liver chemistry.
- **Preferred**: BMI 27.0 or under; BP 134/84 or under and untreated; TC 220 or under with ratio 4.5 or under; A1c 6.0 or under with no diabetes diagnosis; tobacco never or quit over 5 yr; 0 moving violations and no DUI ever; occupation class A; no hazardous avocation; no qualifying family history; no sleep apnea, no alcohol history, normal liver chemistry.
- **Preferred Plus**: BMI 26.0 or under; BP 128/80 or under and untreated; TC 200 or under with ratio 4.0 or under; A1c 5.6 or under with no diabetes diagnosis; tobacco never; 0 moving violations and no DUI ever; occupation class A; no hazardous avocation; no qualifying family history; no sleep apnea, no alcohol history, normal liver chemistry.

Zero debits meeting none of the three is **Standard**.

## 3. Build

Height, weight and BMI are on the file. Read the BMI: up to 18.9 25 | 19.0-27.9 0 | 28.0-30.9 25 | 31.0-33.9 50 | 34.0-36.9 100 | 37.0-39.9 150 | 40.0+ decline.

For a recent change in build, refer to underwriting judgement.

## 4. Blood pressure

Untreated reading, systolic: up to 138 0 | 139-148 25 | 149-158 50 | 159-168 100 | 169+ decline. Diastolic: up to 88 0 | 89-94 25 | 95-99 50 | 100-104 100 | 105+ decline. Charge the worse of the two bands. On treatment: 25.

For a treated condition whose reading is now at target, refer to underwriting judgement.

## 5. Lipids

Total cholesterol: up to 240 0 | 241-280 25 | 281-320 50 | 321+ 75. Total cholesterol to HDL ratio: up to 5.0 0 | 5.1-6.5 25 | 6.6+ 50. Both tables are in force.

Where two tables in this manual point at different bands, refer to underwriting judgement.

## 6. Diabetes and A1c

A1c: up to 6.4 0 | 6.5-6.9 50 | 7.0-7.9 75 | 8.0-8.9 125 | 9.0+ decline. Type 2 diabetes is rated on the A1c. The year of diagnosis and any medication are on the file.

For late-onset metabolic disease that is well controlled, refer to underwriting judgement.

## 7. Tobacco

Never used, or quit more than 5 years ago: non-smoker, 0. Quit 1 to 5 years ago: 25. Current use: smoker rates - in this manual the smoker class runs on the same debit ladder, so add 75 and cap the best available class at Standard. A nicotine-positive laboratory result against a declared *never* makes the applicant a current user.

## 8. Family history

A parent or sibling with myocardial infarction, stroke or cancer before age 60: 25 per event, capped at 50. The applicant's own age does not change the charge.

For applicants well past the family-history qualifying age, refer to underwriting judgement.

## 9. Occupation

Class A (0): office administrator, regional sales manager, software engineer, schoolteacher, pharmacist. Class B (25): delivery driver, site foreman, welder, commercial fisher's deckhand, warehouse supervisor. Class C (50, hazardous): structural steel erector, underground miner, offshore rig hand, logging feller, high-voltage lineman.

## 10. Avocations

For private aviation, refer to underwriting judgement. Where no referral is available, rate private aviation as a hazardous avocation: 50. Scuba, by maximum depth: up to 60 ft 0 | 61-100 ft 25 | 101+ ft 50. Technical rock or ice climbing: 50. Amateur motorsport competition: a flat extra of $5.00 per $1,000.

Where a hazardous occupation and a hazardous avocation appear together, refer to underwriting judgement.

## 11. Driving record

Moving violations in the last 3 years: 0-1 0 | 2 25 | 3+ 50. A DUI conviction: rate 50.

For a recent motoring conviction, refer to underwriting judgement.

## 12. Alcohol and liver

Elevated liver enzymes: 25. A history of treatment for alcohol use: 50.

For borderline liver chemistry, refer to underwriting judgement.

## 13. Sleep apnea

Diagnosed sleep apnea: 50.

For treated sleep-disordered breathing, refer to underwriting judgement.

## 14. Financial underwriting

The face amount applied for, plus cover already in force, should sit within the income multiple for the applicant's age: 18-30 30x | 31-40 25x | 41-50 20x | 51-60 15x | 61+ 10x.

Where the face amount is large relative to income, refer to underwriting judgement.

## 15. Modifiers

A flat extra is charged per $1,000 of face amount in one of three bands: $2.50 / $5.00 / $7.50. An exclusion rider removes one named hazard from cover and carries no charge; name the hazard excluded. Either modifier makes the decision *accept with modification*.

## 16. Where this manual stops

For combinations of cardiac risk factors, refer to underwriting judgement. A referral line means the manual has reached the edge of what it can tell you. Rate the file on what the tables do say, and expect the reviewer to correct you.

# House rule book

_Rewritten after UW-T06. Every entry is reviewer-settled practice from an earlier application in this run (UW-T01, UW-T02, UW-T03, UW-T04, UW-T05, UW-T06). The starter manual still governs anything this book does not cover._

## How to use this book

Work every file in this order.

1. **Postponement checks first** (entries 1 and 2): total cover against the income multiple, and any DUI conviction with its year. If either check trips, the file is postponed: decision `postpone`, rating class null, no modifiers, drivers built under entry 3. Stop there. Do not go on to a class, and do not accept with the problem explained away in the rationale.
2. **Referred items.** List every line of the file that the manual refers to underwriting judgement and check each one against entries 4 to 9. Where an entry applies, follow it instead of the manual's table and instead of your own reasoning. Where no entry applies, rate on the tables and say in the rationale that judgement was used. Where nothing on the file is referred at all, say so in one line and do not manufacture a judgement item.
3. **Tables and class.** Charge each table exactly as written, add the debits, and read the class off the total. On a zero-debit file work the preferred classes under entry 12.
4. **Drivers** under entry 10. The reviewer checks the list of material factors as closely as the class; a correct class with the wrong drivers is still a mismatch.

Six lessons so far about what a referral line means:

- **It is not permission to charge the full table debit.** On UW-T01, charging every referred item at face value made the file two steps too severe. Where the file documents a mitigating fact (treatment compliance, no alcohol history behind a mild enzyme rise), the reviewer credits it; where a hazard can be carved out of cover, the reviewer uses a rider rather than a flat extra.
- **It is not permission to wave the item through.** On UW-T02 the total cover exceeded the income multiple, the manual referred it, and the file was accepted at Standard with a paragraph explaining why the excess was tolerable. The reviewer postponed. Where the referral turns on evidence that is not on the file, the answer is to postpone and ask for it, not to reason your way to an accept.
- **It is not an instruction to add a charge the tables do not carry.** On UW-T03 a mild cardiometabolic cluster (overweight build, low HDL, A1c in the prediabetic range) fell under the referral for combinations of cardiac risk factors. The tables charged build alone; every other reading sat inside its own zero band. Rating on the tables as they stood, with no cluster surcharge, was confirmed correct.
- **It is not a reason to soften a heavy file.** On UW-T04 five cardiac risk factors each sat in a charged band (untreated systolic reading, total cholesterol, lipid ratio, A1c with no diagnosis, mother's MI at 51) alongside a class C occupation. Each was charged on its own table, the debits summed to Table 8, nothing was credited for the absence of a diagnosis or of treatment, nothing was added for the combination, and the reviewer confirmed the file. The combination was acknowledged by naming 'cardiac risk interaction' among the material factors, not by moving the class in either direction.
- **It is not discharged by charging the table rate and writing that judgement was used.** On UW-T06 a DUI convicted two years before the application was charged at the manual's 50, the rationale said judgement had been used, and the clean MVR, normal liver chemistry and absence of any alcohol history were noted as reassurance. The reviewer postponed: a recent DUI is postponed, not rated. Where a referral is about how recent an event is, the missing evidence is time and the record that builds up with it, and nothing on today's file can supply that.
- **A material factor is a factor that carried a charge or forced the decision, and nothing else.** On UW-T05 every table read zero and the file was placed at Preferred. The class was confirmed, but the three readings that kept the applicant out of Preferred Plus (systolic blood pressure, total cholesterol, tobacco quit rather than never) had been listed as drivers, and the reviewer recorded the material factors as none. A reading that only closes a higher preferred class is not a driver; on a zero-debit file the drivers list is empty (entry 12).

So a referred item resolves in one of four ways: **credit** it when the file already documents the mitigating fact; **convert** it to an exclusion rider when the hazard can be removed from cover; **postpone** when the question cannot be answered from the file in front of you, whether because the evidence is missing (UW-T02) or because the event is too recent (UW-T06); **rate on the tables as they stand** when every reading involved is already priced by its own table and the referral is only about how they combine. In the fourth case the referral changes the drivers list (entry 10) and nothing else. Charging at face value, accepting on argument, inventing a surcharge, softening a high total, and rating a recent referred event at its table rate are all wrong.

## 1. Total cover above the income multiple: postpone

**When it applies:** The face amount applied for plus cover already in force exceeds the manual's income multiple for the applicant's age (section 14: 18-30 30x | 31-40 25x | 41-50 20x | 51-60 15x | 61+ 10x). Run this check on every file before rating anything else; the in-force amount counts in full.

**What to do:** Postpone. Decision `postpone`, rating class null, no modifiers. Do not rate the file, and do not accept at any class with the excess explained away in the rationale. Say in the rationale that the file is postponed for financial evidence (justification of the amount, verification of income, purpose of cover) and state the total cover, the multiple and the excess. Name face amount to income among the drivers, together with every other factor the tables would have charged (entry 3).

**Why:** The manual refers a large face amount relative to income to judgement. The reviewer's settled practice is that cover above the multiple is postponed for financial evidence rather than rated: the open question is whether the amount is justified, and nothing on the file can answer it. On UW-T02 (age 40, $1.75M applied plus $250K in force against $68,000 income, a 25x multiple of $1.7M) the excess was roughly a fifth over the multiple, the applicant was otherwise a clean Standard, and the reviewer still postponed. No tolerance margin above the multiple is known to be accepted; do not invent one.

## 2. Recent DUI conviction: postpone

**When it applies:** The file shows a DUI conviction and the conviction is recent. On the one case decided, a conviction two years before the application (convicted 2024, file dated 2026) was recent. Run this check alongside the financial check, before rating anything else. It trips on its own: the rest of the file being clean, the MVR showing no moving violations, the liver chemistry being normal and the alcohol history being empty do not switch it off.

**What to do:** Postpone. Decision `postpone`, rating class null, no modifiers. Do not charge the DUI at the manual's 50 and read a class off the total, and do not accept at any class with a note that judgement was used. In the rationale, set the conviction year against the application date, say the file is postponed for the conviction to age and for the record around it (court disposition, licence status, any alcohol assessment or treatment), and say plainly that the clean MVR, the normal liver chemistry and the absence of a declared alcohol history do not settle the question. Name 'DUI' among the drivers, together with every other factor the tables would have charged (entry 3).

**Boundary:** The manual's 50 for a DUI conviction is the rate for a conviction that is not recent; the referral in section 11 for a recent motoring conviction is what sends a recent one to judgement, and judgement postpones it. Only one point on the line is known: two years is recent. Until a case settles an older conviction, treat a DUI within the last two years as recent and postpone. For an older conviction, charge the manual's 50, name 'DUI' as a driver, and say in the rationale that judgement was used and the conviction was treated as not recent. Ordinary moving violations are charged on their own table in section 11 and have not been referred on any file; do not postpone for them.

**Why:** The manual charges a DUI conviction at 50 but refers a recent motoring conviction to judgement, and the reviewer's settled practice is that a recent DUI is postponed, not rated. On UW-T06 (male 37, 30-year term, $750,000 applied plus $400,000 in force against $175,000 income, inside the multiple; DUI conviction 2024 with no moving violations; normal liver enzymes and no alcohol history; sleep apnea diagnosed with no CPAP in use; every other table at zero) the file was accepted at Table 4 on DUI 50 plus sleep apnea 50. The reviewer's markup: this one needed postponing rather than rating; the material factors are DUI and sleep apnea; a recent DUI is postponed, not rated. Recency is settled by time, and nothing on today's file can stand in for it.

## 3. Drivers on a postponed file

**When it applies:** Any file you postpone, under entry 1 or entry 2.

**What to do:** List as drivers the reason for the postponement and every factor that would have carried a debit had the file been rated. On UW-T02 that was face amount to income and tobacco (quit within five years). On UW-T06 that was DUI and sleep apnea: the DUI forced the postponement, and untreated sleep apnea would have been charged. Rating class stays null and modifiers stay empty. Do not list zero-band readings, credited items, or reassuring facts that did not move the decision; the clean MVR and normal liver chemistry on UW-T06 were not material factors.

**Why:** The reviewer's markup on a postponed file names its material factors as the postponement reason plus the factors that would have rated. A postpone is a deferral, not a clean file; the drivers tell whoever picks the file up again what the rating will turn on once the evidence arrives.

## 4. Hazardous occupation together with a hazardous avocation

**When it applies:** The applicant works in a class C (hazardous) occupation and also carries a hazardous avocation, meaning anything section 10 of the manual would charge: amateur motorsport competition, private aviation, scuba beyond 60 ft, technical rock or ice climbing.

**What to do:** Charge the occupation class debit as the manual sets it. For the avocation, attach an exclusion rider naming the avocation hazard. Do not charge the avocation's flat extra and do not add avocation debits. The rider makes the decision *accept with modification*. Name both the occupation class and the avocation among the drivers: the avocation is still a material factor even though it carries no charge.

**Boundary:** A class C occupation on its own is ordinary rating, not a referred item: charge the class debit, attach no rider, and name occupation class as a driver. UW-T04 (logging feller, no avocation declared) was charged and confirmed that way. A pastime that section 10 does not list (stained-glass work on UW-T04, growing chillies on UW-T05, collecting first-edition crime novels on UW-T06) is not a hazardous avocation; it carries nothing and is not named.

**Why:** The manual refers the occupation-plus-avocation combination to judgement. The reviewer's settled practice is that once one hazardous exposure is already priced through the occupation class, the second is removed from cover rather than charged on top. On UW-T01 (high-voltage lineman plus club saloon racing, 14 events a year) the $5.00 flat extra was struck and replaced by a motorsport exclusion rider.

## 5. Sleep apnea: credited with documented CPAP compliance, charged without it

**When it applies:** Sleep apnea is diagnosed.

**What to do:** Where the file documents CPAP compliance, no debit for sleep apnea and do not list it as a driver. Where the file shows no CPAP in use, or compliance is not documented, charge the manual's 50 and name 'sleep apnea' among the drivers. The charge stands whatever else the file does: on UW-T06 (diagnosed, no CPAP) the reviewer listed sleep apnea as a material factor even though the file was postponed on the DUI.

**Why:** The manual's charge is for diagnosed apnea as such, and it refers treated sleep-disordered breathing to judgement. The reviewer treats documented compliance as a controlled condition carrying no charge, and untreated apnea exactly as the manual writes it. Nothing is credited for an untreated diagnosis, and nothing is added to it.

## 6. Mildly elevated liver enzymes with no alcohol history

**When it applies:** Liver enzymes are elevated but below twice the upper limit of normal, and the file shows no alcohol history and no treatment for alcohol use.

**What to do:** No debit for liver chemistry. Do not list it as a driver.

**Boundary:** Enzymes at or above twice normal, or any alcohol history or treatment, go back to the manual's tables. Normal liver chemistry and an empty alcohol history are the zero state of section 12, not a credit to spend elsewhere: they do not offset a DUI (entry 2), they are not drivers, and they are not reasons to rate a file that should be postponed.

**Why:** The manual refers borderline liver chemistry to judgement. The reviewer treats a mild elevation with no alcohol history as incidental. On UW-T06 the reassurance of normal enzymes and no alcohol history was written into the rationale against a recent DUI, and the reviewer postponed regardless.

## 7. Cardiac risk factors all inside their zero bands: no surcharge, not a driver

**When it applies:** Two or more cardiac risk readings sit together on one file but each is inside a band the manual charges lightly or not at all: BMI in the 28.0-30.9 band; HDL low but the total-cholesterol-to-HDL ratio at or under 5.0; A1c above the preferred thresholds but at or under 6.4 with no diabetes diagnosis; blood pressure untreated and at or under 138/88. Section 16 refers combinations of cardiac risk factors to judgement, so this cluster is a referred item.

**What to do:** Charge exactly what each table charges and nothing more. Add no cluster debit and no flat extra, and do not postpone for further tests. Read the class off the total as usual; a single table debit closes all three preferred classes, so build at the 28.0-30.9 band with everything else clean is Standard. Name as drivers only the factors that actually carried a debit; do not list the zero-charge readings and do not list the interaction. Say in the rationale that the cluster was considered under judgement and that nothing was added beyond the table charges.

**Boundary:** Do not invoke this entry to describe a file that has nothing abnormal on it. On UW-T05 every reading sat comfortably inside its zero band (BMI 24.9, BP 133/72 untreated, TC 217 with ratio 3.8, A1c 5.2), no cluster question was raised, and the file was a clean file under entry 12. On UW-T06 a BMI of 26.4 and an A1c of 5.7 with everything else clean raised no cluster question either. Where the readings cross into charged bands, entry 8 applies instead.

**Why:** On UW-T03 (male 38, BMI 29.3 stable, HDL 38 with ratio 4.6, A1c 6.2, BP 128/71 untreated, otherwise clean) the file was rated on build alone and accepted at Standard, and the reviewer confirmed it with build the only material factor. A referral about a combination does not manufacture a charge no table carries.

## 8. Cardiac risk factors each in a charged band: charge every table, sum, read the class, name the interaction

**When it applies:** More than one of the cardiac risk tables charges on the same file: untreated blood pressure at 139 systolic or 89 diastolic or above; total cholesterol above 240; total-cholesterol-to-HDL ratio above 5.0; A1c 6.5 or above; a parent or sibling MI or stroke before 60; build in a charged band. This is the combinations-of-cardiac-risk-factors referral with real debits behind it.

**What to do:** Charge each reading on its own table exactly as written, add the debits together with everything else on the file, and read the class off the total. Then:

- Add nothing for the combination: no cluster debit, no flat extra, no step up the table ladder.
- Take nothing off either. An A1c in a charged band with no diabetes diagnosis is charged on the A1c table; the absence of a diagnosis is not a credit, and the manual's referral for well-controlled late-onset metabolic disease is about diagnosed, treated disease, not an undiagnosed elevated reading. An untreated reading in a charged band is charged as a reading; the absence of treatment is not a credit. A parent's MI before 60 is charged whatever the applicant's age, unless the applicant is well past the qualifying age.
- Do not postpone for repeat readings or confirmatory tests when the readings are on the file, and do not decline on judgement while the total sits below the decline band. A high table class is the right answer to a heavy file.
- Say in the rationale that the cardiac risk-factor combination was considered under judgement and that nothing was added or credited beyond the table charges.
- Name every charged factor among the drivers, one per table, and add 'cardiac risk interaction' as a further driver (entry 10).

**Why:** On UW-T04 (female 37, untreated 139/83, total cholesterol 256 with ratio 5.6, A1c 6.6 with no diagnosis, mother's MI at 51, logging feller class C, otherwise clean, cover inside the multiple) the debits summed to Table 8 and the file was accepted at that class. The reviewer confirmed it as correct and listed the material factors as blood pressure reading, total cholesterol, lipid ratio, A1c, family history, occupation class and cardiac risk interaction. The reviewer's practice is therefore that each reading is priced by its own table, the combination itself moves the class in neither direction, and the interaction is recorded as a factor rather than a charge. Only two cases anchor the boundary for naming it: none of the cardiac tables charged on UW-T03 and the interaction was not named; five charged on UW-T04 and it was. Treat two or more charged cardiac tables as enough to name it until a case says otherwise.

## 9. Both lipid tables charge, and each is named on its own

**When it applies:** Total cholesterol is above 240 and the total-cholesterol-to-HDL ratio is above 5.0 on the same file.

**What to do:** Charge the total cholesterol table and the ratio table both, cumulatively; the manual says both tables are in force. List 'total cholesterol' and 'lipid ratio' as two separate drivers, not one 'lipids' driver. Where only one lipid table charges, name only that one. Where neither charges, name neither, even if the total cholesterol closed a preferred class (entry 12).

**Boundary:** On UW-T04 both readings fell in the first charged band of their tables, so the manual's referral for two tables pointing at different bands did not arise. Where the two lipid tables land in different bands, no practice is settled yet: rate on both tables as they stand and say judgement was used.

**Why:** On UW-T04 (total cholesterol 256, ratio 5.6) both were charged and the reviewer named total cholesterol and lipid ratio as separate material factors. The two tables measure different things and the reviewer tracks them separately; folding them into one driver understates the factor count the reviewer records.

## 10. Naming drivers

**When it applies:** Every file.

**What to do:** The drivers are the material factors the reviewer will list, so build them the same way:

- One driver per table that carried a debit, named by the factor and not the number: 'blood pressure reading' for an untreated reading in a charged band (the reviewer's own phrase), 'total cholesterol', 'lipid ratio', 'A1c', 'family history', 'occupation class', 'build', 'tobacco', 'sleep apnea', 'DUI' (the reviewer's own word, for a conviction whether rated or postponed), and so on.
- Add 'cardiac risk interaction' when entry 8 applies, that is when more than one cardiac risk table charged. Do not add it when the cardiac readings all sit in zero bands (entry 7).
- On a postponed file, add the postponement reason and keep every factor that would have rated (entry 3).
- Where an avocation has been converted to an exclusion rider, name the avocation even though it carries no charge (entry 4).
- Never list a reading that carried no debit, a credited item (entries 5 and 6), a reading that only closed a higher preferred class (entry 12), or an incidental detail the tables do not reach (a hobby section 10 does not list, a stable weight, a clean driving record, a negative nicotine screen, normal liver chemistry, an empty alcohol history).
- When no table charged, the file is not postponed and no rider is attached, the list is empty. Send an empty list. Do not fill it with the criteria that decided between Preferred Plus, Preferred and Standard Plus; those belong in the rationale, not in the drivers.

**Why:** The reviewer's markup on every file so far has listed the material factors explicitly: build alone on UW-T03; face amount to income plus tobacco on UW-T02; seven factors on UW-T04; none on UW-T05; DUI and sleep apnea on UW-T06. The class has been confirmed while the drivers were wrong in both directions. On UW-T04 I gave too few: 'lipids' as one factor where the reviewer counted two, and no 'cardiac risk interaction'. On UW-T05 I gave too many: three readings that carried no debit, named only because they closed Preferred Plus. On UW-T06 the two drivers matched the reviewer's, but the decision did not; a right drivers list is necessary, not sufficient.

## 11. Cover inside the income multiple: no financial referral, but not a clean bill either

**When it applies:** Face amount applied for plus cover already in force is at or under the income multiple for the applicant's age.

**What to do:** State in one line of the rationale that the total cover sits inside the multiple, then run the second postponement check (entry 2) and go on to the medical and lifestyle tables. Do not treat the financial section as a judgement item, do not name face amount to income as a driver, and do not postpone for financial evidence. The size of the face amount on its own does not change this: a seven-figure face amount inside the multiple is rated like any other. Passing the financial check clears only the financial question; it does not clear the file.

**Why:** The manual's referral in section 14 is only for a face amount that is large relative to income. On UW-T03 ($750,000 applied, nothing in force, against $175,000 income at age 38), UW-T04 ($250,000 applied plus $250,000 in force, against $260,000 income at age 37), UW-T05 ($1,000,000 applied plus $250,000 in force, against $260,000 income at age 29, inside the 30x multiple of $7.8M) and UW-T06 ($750,000 applied plus $400,000 in force, $1.15M against a 25x multiple of $4.375M at age 37) the total was inside the multiple and no financial question arose. The first three were rated on the other tables and confirmed; UW-T06 was postponed on the DUI instead, which is why the two postponement checks are run independently. Entry 1 applies only when the multiple is exceeded.

## 12. Zero-debit file: read the preferred class off its criteria, and the drivers are none

**When it applies:** Every table in sections 3 to 13 reads zero, whether outright or because a referred item was credited under entries 5 or 6; neither postponement check trips (entries 1 and 2); no modifier is in play.

**What to do:** Decision `accept`. Work the three preferred classes from the top. Preferred Plus needs every one of its criteria met, including tobacco never; Preferred needs every one of its own; Standard Plus likewise; zero debits meeting none of the three is Standard. A single criterion missed closes that class, however clean the rest of the file, and the applicant falls to the next class down whose criteria are all met. Tobacco quit more than five years ago is a non-smoker at zero debits and is eligible for Preferred and Standard Plus, but never for Preferred Plus. In the rationale, state the class reached and, if useful, which criteria closed the class above. Then send `drivers` as an empty list. Do not name the closing criteria, do not name the zero-band readings, and do not name the absence of judgement items. Modifiers stay empty.

**Why:** On UW-T05 (male 29, whole life, $1,000,000 applied with $250,000 in force against $260,000 income; BMI 24.9 and stable; BP 133/72 untreated; TC 217 with ratio 3.8; A1c 5.2; no family history; pharmacist class A; no avocation; clean MVR; normal liver and no alcohol history; no apnea; tobacco quit over five years with a negative nicotine screen) every table read zero. Preferred Plus was closed by the systolic reading, the total cholesterol and the tobacco history; every Preferred criterion was met. Preferred was confirmed correct and the reviewer recorded the material factors as none. The class on a clean file is decided by the preferred criteria; the drivers record only charges and decision-forcing facts, and on a clean file there are none. Naming the criteria that separated Preferred from Preferred Plus was the one error on the file.

your_answer.rationale: Total cover $1.4M sits inside the 15x multiple ($3.9M); no DUI. No line of the file is referred to judgement.
